description: D4 CRITICAL — close the latent licence defect by moving corpus tiering from publication to INGEST (docs/DECISION-D4-CLDF-AND-WIKIBASE.md §4; ADOPT-DECIDE-REGISTER F5). The machinery exists but sits at the wrong end of the pipe: contracts/egress-policy.json declares `enforcedAt: "pack-construction"` with `licensePolicy.allowedSpdxClasses: ["CC0","CC-BY"]`, and the per-record SPDX licence on a lexicon-derived row is not stored at all — data/source/lexicons/*.tsv has NO `license` column, so scripts/export-for-engine.ts DERIVES one at export time from the row's `source` cell via `licenseForSource`/`DEFAULT_LICENSE`. Three consequences, all real today: (1) a curated row whose content actually came from a share-alike or non-commercial upstream but whose `source` reads `pinakes` is stamped the permissive default and passes the CC0/CC-BY filter unchallenged; (2) graph-side share-alike (PHOIBLE + kaikki/Wiktionary, both CC-BY-SA-3.0) and non-commercial (Seshat, `license: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0` in engine/inputs/categories/seshat-polities.yml) records enter the same corpus as the permissive core and are only partitioned later, by engine/src/pinakes_engine/schema/license_class.py at package time; (3) obligations propagate off-repo — pinakes -> lugh's training corpus -> trained models, and pinakes -> insimul synthetic worlds — so a mis-stamped row is not recoverable by a downstream filter. Fix the direction of enforcement: a record acquires its SPDX licence and its tier AT ADMISSION, the tier is STORED (never re-derived), an unregistered licence is fail-closed `unknown`, and the publication-side filter stays as defence-in-depth rather than as the only gate. Scope: contracts (egress-policy + canonical schema licence column), the engine acquire/write-back admission path, the lexicon TSVs' new licence column + backfill, the exporters, and the docs. Head of the D4 chain — 113/114/118/122 depend on it.

userStories.title: A stored per-row licence + tier on the lexicon corpus, not a derived one
userStories.description: Give data/source/lexicons/*.tsv a first-class SPDX licence column and a derived-once-then-stored corpus tier, so a row's redistribution class is data rather than an inference from its `source` cell at export time. Backfill every existing row from the ATTRIBUTION.md source table, and make the export path READ the column instead of calling licenseForSource.
acceptanceCriteria: The canonical schema (contracts/canonical-schema.json, regenerated bindings via `bun run gen:contracts`) and the lexicon TSV header both carry a per-row SPDX `license` column; `bun run check:contracts` (the drift gate) is green and no generated file was hand-edited.

Every existing lexicon row is backfilled with an explicit SPDX id justified against docs/ATTRIBUTION.md's per-file source table — rows whose upstream is genuinely mixed or unverified are stamped with the fail-closed `unknown` sentinel rather than the permissive default, and the count of `unknown` rows is recorded in docs/corpus-tier-report.md as the curation backlog.

scripts/export-for-engine.ts reads the stored `license` column as the source of truth and only falls back to `licenseForSource` for a blank cell (a fallback that is itself reported, not silent); `DEFAULT_LICENSE` no longer silently stamps a permissive class onto an unstamped row.
`bun run convergence-qa` and `.chief/verify.sh` pass, with the pinned snapshots the schema/data change cascades into regenerated per scripts/CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Admission-time licence gate on the acquire/write-back path
userStories.description: Make the acquire -> reconcile -> write-back cascade classify and gate on licence BEFORE a record lands, using engine/src/pinakes_engine/schema/license_class.py as the classifier. A record with no registered licence never enters the corpus; a share-alike or non-commercial record enters a distinct tier partition, never the permissive core.
acceptanceCriteria: The write-back / normalize path refuses to land a record whose SPDX id classifies `unknown` (unregistered = all-rights-reserved), reporting the rejection with the source and id rather than dropping it silently — proven by a test that feeds an unregistered licence through and asserts the refusal.

Admitted records are partitioned into stored tiers at admission: the permissive core (public-domain + attribution), a distinct `share-alike` overlay (PHOIBLE, kaikki/Wiktionary, DBpedia — CC-BY-SA), and a quarantined `non-commercial` partition (Seshat, CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0), so no later step has to re-derive which duty a row carries; a test asserts a CC-BY-NC-SA record can never reach the core partition.

Edge records carry the licence too, closing the gap documented in engine/src/pinakes_engine/schema/CLAUDE.md (`_carry_edge_provenance` copies source/source_url/retrieved_at/confidence but leaves the declared `license` cell blank) — an edge inherits its source record's licence, or the most restrictive of its two endpoints where it is linker-derived, with the rule stated in the docstring and pinned by a test.
`uv run --all-packages pytest -q engine/tests` and the engine gate (`uv run ruff check .` + `uv run mypy src` from engine/) are green.

userStories.title: Re-point the policy at ingest and prove the downstream propagation is contained
userStories.description: Update contracts/egress-policy.json so ingest is the enforcement point and pack-construction is defence-in-depth, then prove the two off-repo propagation paths D4 names — lugh's training corpus and insimul's synthetic worlds — cannot receive a tier they are not entitled to.
acceptanceCriteria: contracts/egress-policy.json's `enforcedAt` names ingest as the primary enforcement point with pack-construction retained as a second gate, the `licensePolicy` block documents the stored-tier vocabulary, and `egress-policy.test.ts` still asserts `licensePolicyFor(allowedSpdxClasses)` reproduces `allowedClasses` exactly (no drift between contracts/kgp.ts and the policy).

The lugh corpus-export cascade (pinakes-export-triples / -verbalizations / -kgqa, per scripts/CLAUDE.md) and scripts/export-insimul-pack.ts both select on the STORED tier rather than re-deriving a class, and each emits a manifest block naming the tiers included and excluded — a test asserts that a share-alike or non-commercial row present in the corpus is absent from a permissive-core export and accounted for in the excluded tally.

docs/ATTRIBUTION.md's 'License-partitioned redistribution' section is rewritten to describe ingest-time tiering (what is admitted, into which tier, and what each tier may leave the repo as), and states plainly that the obligation attaches at admission because a downstream consumer cannot undo a mis-stamped row.
`.chief/verify.sh` passes and `bun run convergence-qa` is green on the re-tiered corpus.
